To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have measured Hα velocity fields in a sample of 26 nearby low-mass disk galaxies, that we have compared the Hα velocity fields to CO velocity fields for 11 galaxies and found them to be in good overall agreement, and that we have derived rotation curves for these galaxies that we will use to determine their mass profiles in a companion paper.
we have measured H$\alpha$ rotation curves in 26 low-mas galaxies and that the kinematic properties of the H$\alpha$, CO, and stellar emission are in good agreement.
we have obtained high-resolution H$\alpha$ maps of 26 low mass galaxies and have compared these to CO maps of 11 of the galaxies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dark matter distribution and the formation of dwarf galaxies.
the study of dwarf galaxies and the dark matter distribution within them.
the dark matter distributions in low-mass disk galaxies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the dark matter distribution in low-mass disk galaxies can be described by the cusp profile.
the H$\alpha$, H{\sc i}, and CO kinematics of these galaxies are all in agreement.
we do not have enough evidence to make a strong statement on the dark matter distribution in the inner regions of low-mass disk galaxies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dark matter halos of dwarf galaxies are diverse in their inner slopes, with a range of slopes from $\sim -1.5$ to $\sim -2.5$, and with a median slope of $\sim -1$.
the rotation curves of our sample show a wide diversity of slopes.
the dark matter distribution in low-mass disk galaxies is still a mystery.
The main takeaway from our work is that
H$\alpha$ is a robust and efficient tracer of the kinematics of low-mass disk galaxies.
the H$\alpha$, CO, and stellar velocity fields are consistent, and thus, we can use the H$\alpha$/CO velocity field as a robust tracer of the dark matter distribution.
the dark matter profiles of low-mass disk galaxies are diverse and cannot be described by a single density profile.
